slice.probe: Test GitHub GraphQL updateRefs as an atomic two-ref scheduled-Chat protocol using beforeOid on both refs and force=false; then model the same force-capable dual-rewrite adversary and separately classify current scheduled-Chat callability.

source_refs.claim: updateRefs applies a list of RefUpdate operations atomically; if one is rejected no ref is modified; beforeOid is an expected-current precondition; force=true allows non-fast-forward updates.
The exposed GitHub connector surface contains singular update_ref/create_branch operations but no generic GraphQL updateRefs multi-ref mutation; generic fetch is GET-only.

model.protocol_result: If W1 is accepted first, both refs move together to A1/B1. W2 then fails an expected-current precondition and, because the mutation is atomic, neither stale ref update is applied. The separate-REST torn-update and partial-commit window is therefore removed for protocol-compliant participants.

force_capable_actor.result: A coherent atomic rewind of both mutable refs remains possible when force-capable authority is available; atomicity prevents tearing but does not create an independently monotonic rollback anchor.

findings: Atomic beforeOid checks across both refs collapse the stale-sibling, torn-update and partial-protocol-commit classes for compliant writers.
The guarantee is limited to Git ref state participating in one updateRefs mutation; it does not make unrelated external side effects transactional.
Atomicity does not solve coherent history rewrite by an actor allowed to force-move both mutable refs.

The current scheduled-Chat GitHub connector does not expose updateRefs or a generic GraphQL mutation surface, so this mechanism cannot currently count as an executable Phase-1 route despite requiring no finite monthly quota or incremental monetary cost in the abstract protocol model.

single_shared_ref_non_force.remaining_gap: shared serialization hotspot and no independent rollback anchor

protected_or_external_monotonic_witness.remaining_gap: would introduce protected-authority or external/quota assumptions unless independently eliminated

slice.tested_scope: One bounded CLEAN information-flow/concurrency model for two Git refs under GitHub's documented updateRefs semantics, two compliant simultaneous writers from common heads, one stale rejected writer, one force-capable coherent dual-ref rewind, and current connector tool-surface discovery. No live ref mutation, O/downstream/other-worker semantics, protected/admin mutation, hosted compute/storage add-on, external model/API execution, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, manual execution, scheduler mutation, same-run retry, or optional second leaf.
slice.conflict_check: Exactly one bounded CLEAN Phase-1 child; only own role-local state/receipt namespaces are mutated. No O, downstream, other-role state, scheduler, protected authority, or unrelated repository semantics consumed as exploration input.

frontier: Atomic multi-ref beforeOid CAS removes the separate-REST torn-update and partial-protocol-commit class for compliant writers.
The current scheduled-Chat connector does not expose that atomic multi-ref operation, so protocol existence is not execution parity.
A force-capable actor can still coherently rewind both mutable refs; an independently monotonic authority/retention domain remains the rollback-detection boundary.

The highest-value exposed-surface alternative is now a single-ref transaction record that encodes both logical state and witness linkage inside one immutable commit and uses only the available non-force update_ref path.
